claims.text: The concept of algorithmic fairness was largely unfamiliar to participants from marginalized populations.
Learning about algorithmic unfairness elicited negative feelings among participants that connect to national discussions about racial injustice and economic inequality.
Participants expressed concerns about potential harms from algorithmic systems to themselves and society.
Perceptions of algorithmic fairness or unfairness can substantially affect user trust in a company or product.

evidence.description: While the concept of algorithmic fairness was largely unfamiliar
learning about algorithmic (un)fairness elicited negative feelings that connect to current national discussions about racial injustice and economic inequality.
In addition to their concerns about potential harms to themselves and society
participants also indicated that algorithmic fairness (or lack thereof) could substantially affect their trust in a company or product.

methodologies.name: Qualitative Workshops and Interviews
methodologies.description: Conducted workshops and interviews with 44 participants from populations marginalized by race or class in the United States to explore perceptions of algorithmic fairness.
